newsitem.title: GAMBIA: Gambian president sacks finance, foreign ministers.
newsitem.headline: Gambian president sacks finance, foreign ministers.

text.p: Gambian President Yahya Jammeh sacked his finance and foreign ministers on Friday when he made his first cabinet appointments as civilian leader.

The cabinet announced on state radio comprises 13 members, each with the new title of Secretary of State in line with a new constitution that returned the West African state to democracy in January after two years of military rule.

Foreign Minister Blaise Jagne was replaced by Omar Njie while the Finance and Economy Portfolio passed from Bala Garba Jahumpa to Dominic Mendy. A third minister dropped was Amina Faal Sonko, for Youth and Sports.

Another feature of the new cabinet was the appointment of former vice-president Edward Singateh to the new post of Secretary of State in the president's office, with responsibility for the National Assembly, the civil service, fisheries and natural resources.
Political analysts said Singateh, a retired army captain and one of the officers who staged a 1994 coup with Jammeh, also a captain at the time, would effectively remain vice-president.
Singateh, 30, cannot be named vice-president because of a constitutional requirement that the holder be at least 31.

Jammeh led the June 1994 coup that toppled the elected government founding president Sir Dawda Jawara, now exiled in Britain. He successfully contested elections last September and his party also won a commanding majority in parliamentary polls in December.
